# Honey extraction day

Log for Saturday 23 August 2025, done in the kitchen with Alfie.

- 06:40 Clearer boards went on Primrose, Bramble and Hazel on Thursday. Ivy left alone, not enough to spare.
- 07:15 Supers off. 9 supers in total: Primrose 4, Bramble 3, Hazel 2. Into the car under damp tea towels.
- 07:50 Kitchen sealed: windows shut, every surface covered in newspaper and cling film. Any bee or wasp that gets in will tell the others.
- 08:10 Extractor collected from the association, a 4-frame tangential, hire ref TVB-EX-04, £10 for the weekend, deposit £20.
- 08:30 Refractometer check on three frames: 17.6%, 17.9%, 18.1%. Under 18.5%, fine to extract.
- 08:45 Uncapping with the bread knife warmed in a jug of hot water. Cappings into the sieve over the bucket.
- 09:00 to 13:30 Spinning. 4 frames a go, 3 minutes a side at low speed, then flip and finish fast. Alfie on the handle, me uncapping.
- 11:20 Tea and digestives. Alfie's hands sticky to the wrist.
- 13:45 Through the double sieve (1000 and 400 micron) into two 30 lb buckets with honey gates.
- 14:30 Weighed: 41.2 lb in total. Down on 2024 (48 lb) because of the wet June.
- 15:00 Supers back on the hives at dusk to be licked clean.
- Sunday 24th: settled overnight, skimmed the froth, jarred. 58 one-pound jars, labels "Lustleigh Orchard Honey, batch LO-25-1".
- Monday: extractor washed in cold water first (hot melts the wax into a glue) and returned. Deposit back.

Notes for next year:

- Book the extractor by June, three people wanted it that weekend
- Buy a second uncapping fork, the knife is slow
- 20 jars set aside for the stall, see [[Bake sale 2025 notes]], sold at £7 each, all gone by 11 am
- Cappings wax rendered in the solar melter for the [[Winterizing the hive]] jobs list
